subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Model Predictive Control: Planning Ahead
description: A short lesson to help you apply Model Predictive Control: Planning Ahead.

hook.text: MPC looks into the future — it simulates many possible actions and picks the best sequence.

buildup.text: At each step, MPC solves an optimization problem over a prediction horizon — then applies only the first action.

discovery.text: It naturally handles constraints — valve limits, speed limits, temperature bounds — in the optimization.

twist.text: MPC needs significant computation. Faster processors and better algorithms now make it real-time capable.

climax.text: Chemical plants, autonomous vehicles, and building energy management all run on MPC.

punchline.text: Look ahead, optimize, act, repeat — MPC decides optimally each step.

quiz.question: What is a unique advantage of MPC over PID control?
options: MPC requires no mathematical model of the system
MPC can directly incorporate constraints like actuator limits into its optimization
MPC uses simpler calculations than PID
